title: Osero's Facilitator and GovOps functions are supplied by an external Executor Agent through the Executor Accord Primitive
content:
Osero's Executor Accord Primitive is `Active` (A.6.1.1.7.2.2.1.1.1) with one live Instance named Ozone. The Instance's sole substantive parameter, A.6.1.1.7.2.2.1.2.1.1.1, does not define the roles but delegates them: "The Operational Facilitator and Operational GovOps for Ozone are specified in A.6.1.2.2 - Operational Executor Agent Ozone."

This is the structural counterpart to the Root Edit protocol. Every gate in that protocol — the alignment finding, the feasibility confirmation, the trigger of the Snapshot poll, the submission of the approved edit — is exercised by an actor Osero does not contain and whose specification lives in a different Agent's Artifact.

The separation buys independence: a Facilitator supplied under an Accord by a dedicated Executor Agent is not an employee of the entity whose proposals they screen, which is precisely what makes the alignment gate credible rather than self-certifying. It also allows one Executor Agent to serve multiple Primes with a consistent standard.

The dependency runs the other way too. Osero's ability to amend its own Artifact is contingent on the Accord remaining active and on Ozone continuing to supply functioning role-holders. Because the Accord is an Operational Primitive with Suspended and Failed states, that supply is revocable — Osero's governance can in principle be stalled by events in an Artifact its own token holders do not control.
description: The Ozone Instance points at A.6.1.2.2 for who fills these roles, so the actor gatekeeping Osero governance sits outside Osero and is governed by its own Artifact.
